title: Emergency Diesel Firewater System
model_title: Emergency Diesel-Driven Firewater Pump System (Horizontal Split-Case Pump)

introduction.definition: An emergency diesel firewater system is a fire pump driven by a dedicated diesel engine so firefighting water is available even if electrical power fails. The listed controller starts it automatically when fire-main pressure falls; it delivers rated flow at rated pressure to hydrants, monitors and sprinklers. A jockey pump keeps the main pressurised.
applications: Refinery, chemical, power and alumina plant fire mains
key_points: 150 % of rated flow at ≥ 65 % of rated pressure (NFPA 20 style)
Two battery sets; weekly run test

pressure.title: Rated flow at rated pressure — guaranteed
pressure.description: Fire pumps are certified to deliver rated flow at rated pressure, at least 150 % of rated flow at not less than 65 % of rated pressure, with churn (shut-off) pressure not above 140 % of rated (NFPA 20 style rules — verify against the governing edition). The diesel driver gives independence from the electrical supply; it starts automatically on a pressure drop, has two battery sets, and is tested weekly. The jockey pump makes up small leaks so the main pump starts only for a real demand.

foundation: Level concrete plinth; anchor the skid; bund or drain for chemical / oil spills.
alignment: Skid level; check pump–motor alignment where not close-coupled; supports so piping loads do not reach equipment nozzles.
piping: Isolation valves and bypass for maintenance; drains and vents; correct materials for the chemical; label lines and flow direction.
commissioning: Pressure-test piping; flush; check rotation and interlocks; calibrate instruments; run on water before chemicals.

safety: Exhaust, hot surfaces, rotating parts; never leave in "off" without impairment procedure.

video_tutorials.title: Emergency Diesel Firewater System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Emergency Diesel Firewater System.
An emergency diesel firewater system is a fire pump driven by a dedicated diesel engine so firefighting water is available even if electrical power fails.
The listed controller starts it automatically when fire-main pressure falls; it delivers rated flow at rated pressure to hydrants, monitors and sprinklers.
A jockey pump keeps the main pressurised.
Typical applications include refinery, chemical, power and alumina plant fire mains; large buildings and tank farms.

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Radiator Fan (engine driven), Crankshaft Output, Flywheel, Drive Shaft & Flexible Coupling (turning), Horizontal Split-Case Fire Pump Casing (axially split; side suction & discharge), Double-Suction Impeller & Pump Shaft (turning).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Emergency Diesel Firewater System — Operation

script.narration: How the Emergency Diesel Firewater System works.
Pressure drops when a hydrant or sprinkler opens.
The controller starts the diesel engine.
The engine drives the split-case pump.
The impeller raises pressure.
Water goes to the fire main; the relief valve limits pressure.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

Fire pumps are certified to deliver rated flow at rated pressure, at least 150 % of rated flow at not less than 65 % of rated pressure, with churn (shut-off) pressure not above 140 % of rated (NFPA 20 style rules — verify against the governing edition).

video_tutorials.title: Emergency Diesel Firewater System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Emergency Diesel Firewater System.
Weekly no-flow run; check batteries, fuel, oil, coolant.
Annual flow test through the test header.
Engine overhaul per hours; pump wear rings.
Watch for fails to start: controller alarm. Common cause: flat batteries, no fuel, starter fault.
Watch for low pressure at rated flow: test shows low curve. Common cause: wear rings worn, suction problem.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
